newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK, U.S. PARTNERS STILL NEGOTIATING GSM VENTURE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK, U.S. PARTNERS STILL NEGOTIATING GSM VENTURE.

text.p: Slovak state-run telephone monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST) on Friday said it has still not reached an agreement with its U.S. partners over conditions for creating an operator for a GSM network.
But Igor Huzevka, the ST consultant for the venture told Reuters that both sides are continuing negotiations on the final composition of the firm.
"Today we will have a further round of talks with our U.S. partners on setting up a new joint-stock company that to operate the GSM system," he said.
On September 4, the Ministry of Telecommunications formally granted a GSM licence to Eurotel, a joint venture between ST, U.S. West Inc and Bell Atlantic Corp.
The firms are negotiating the final makeup of the venture since tender conditions for the GSM (Global System for Mobile) licence state the operator must be at least 60 percent Slovak.
ST holds 51 percent of Eurotel, which operates the country's sole mobile telephone network, the NMT lower frequency analogue system, while the two U.S. telecom groups have the remaining 49 percent.
The ministry said the three partners in Eurotel had 90 days from the date it issued the licence to officially create a joint-stock company conforming to the tender conditions.
The ministry said it did not expect the Eurotel owners to fail to agree on creating the operator, but warned that if they do not meet the deadline they might lose the licence.
Talks on the ownership structure have dragged on for months. In July ST said it had agreed in principle with its two U.S. partners to create the new company.
ST said negotiations concentrated mainly on executive rights in the new company and the split of investments. It ruled out any changes to the make-up of the group.
A second licence has been granted to Slovtel, a consortium of four Slovak energy companies, the state monopoly gas distributor and a private firm Hanco sro, which teamed up with France Telecom.
